name: Hummingbird cake
origin: A Southern United States spice cake with banana, pineapple and pecans, its recipe printed in Southern Living magazine in 1978 after being submitted by a reader in North Carolina; named, by tradition, for being as sweet as the nectar hummingbirds feed on.

ingredients.note: oil-based, like carrot cake; see catalog.ts module notes on the missing vegetable-oil substance record
water fraction of mashed banana at 60% of flour mass, split as in banana-cake.json
water fraction of crushed, drained pineapple at 40% of flour mass, split by USDA canned-pineapple composition (~86% water)

process.name: whisk oil, sugar and eggs
process.description: whisk oil, sugar and eggs together

process.name: fold in fruit and dry
process.description: fold in flour, leavening, salt and spice, then the mashed banana, crushed pineapple and pecans

notes: Both banana and pineapple are split by their own real water content (USDA FoodData Central: raw banana ~74.9%, canned pineapple ~86% water), the same technique used in carrot-cake.json and banana-cake.json, so their real hydration contribution is honestly credited rather than treated as inert bulk. The cream-cheese frosting traditionally finishing this cake is out of scope, as in carrot-cake.json.
